companyArtifacts.content:
Launch page — current message
Headline: “Somebody: an AI manager for your business.”
Subhead: “Automate your workflows with AI.”
Status: launch not converting; visitors leave without signing up.
Assumed audience: generic “businesses”.
Assumed pain point: “too many tools”.

Verified launch baseline (req_01)
Intended audience and context: The relaunch is intended to convert one-person-company founders. The company builds Somebody for one-person companies and lean SMEs; the current page instead uses the generic audience label “businesses.”
Performance signal: Internal launch context reports low signup conversion and that visitors do not recognise themselves.
Known constraint: No paid spend without an explicit application-approved provider path.
Diagnostic note: The current message and assumed audience are retained above as the existing baseline; the verified context indicates a founder-specific audience should be addressed in diagnosis.
Source: company record launch/context, observed as ev_1790045033627_hyxp0v.

Underperformance diagnosis and relaunch implications (req_02)
Evidence-supported material cause: audience/message mismatch. The current headline addresses a generic “business” audience, while the intended relaunch audience is one-person-company founders. The relaunch should make the founder recognise their situation immediately, state the job Somebody takes on, and give a clear low-friction next step.

Revised relaunch messaging package (req_03)
Primary headline: “Run your one-person company with an AI manager.”
Primary subhead: “Somebody keeps the work moving—so you can spend less time coordinating tools, tasks, and follow-ups and more time running the business.”
Recognition line: “Built for founders doing the selling, delivery, admin, and follow-up themselves.”
Value points:
- Turn scattered business work into a clear set of next actions.
- Keep routine follow-ups and operating tasks moving without adding another manager.
- Get practical support across the work a lean company must do every day.
Primary CTA: “Try Somebody”
Secondary CTA: “See how it works”
CTA expectation: The primary CTA should lead directly to the existing signup or trial flow; the secondary CTA should lead to a concise explanation of the workflow and product experience.
Alternate headline options for controlled testing:
A. “Your AI manager for the work behind the business.”
B. “One-person company? Let Somebody run the follow-through.”
Messaging guardrail: Do not claim guaranteed outcomes, full automation, or capabilities not confirmed by the product. Keep “AI manager” as the category description and explain the benefit in concrete founder language.
Assumptions to validate: the product supports the described workflow and follow-up use cases; “Try Somebody” is the correct available conversion path; the audience responds better to “one-person company” than generic “business”; and the secondary CTA destination exists.

Execution-ready launch specification (req_04)
Page order:
1. Primary headline and subhead.
2. Recognition line immediately below the hero.
3. Primary and secondary CTAs.
4. Three value points, using concrete founder language.
5. Short “how it works” explanation with no unsupported capability claims.
6. Repeat the primary CTA.

Consistency checks:
- Audience is consistently “one-person-company founders” (with lean SMEs as adjacent context), not generic “businesses.”
- Problem is consistently operational overload and follow-through, not merely “too many tools.”
- Product role is consistently an AI manager that helps keep work moving; copy must not imply autonomous control beyond verified product capability.
- CTA language and the stated signup objective are aligned.
- The message distinguishes the current baseline from the relaunch and does not present the low-conversion signal as a product promise.

Unresolved material decisions before publishing:
- Confirm the exact signup/trial destination and whether “Try Somebody” is the approved CTA label.
- Confirm which workflow and follow-up capabilities are live; remove any value point not supported by the current product.
- Choose the primary headline and, if testing is possible, define the allocation and test duration without paid spend.
- Confirm whether “one-person company” is the preferred audience term in the page implementation.
- Confirm the measurement owner and the event instrumentation for CTA clicks, signup starts, and completed signups.

Measurement relative to the current launch:
Baseline: the current launch has low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves; the current message uses generic “businesses.”
Primary success measure: completed signup conversion rate from page visitors, compared with the current launch baseline over the same measurement window.
Diagnostic measures: hero-to-CTA click-through rate, signup-start rate, completed-signup rate, and drop-off between signup start and completion. Report absolute rates and percentage-point change versus baseline, not only relative lift.
Recognition check: use a short on-page or user-research prompt to test whether visitors identify themselves as one-person-company founders; this is diagnostic, not a substitute for signup conversion.
Decision rule: before launch, record the current baseline window, denominator, traffic source, and instrumentation. After the relaunch, compare the same definitions and window. If conversion improves without a recognition improvement, revisit message clarity; if recognition improves without conversion improvement, inspect CTA, flow, and product-fit friction. Do not claim success until the baseline and post-launch definitions are comparable.
Constraint and operating plan: use owned resources and organic/internal testing only unless an explicit application-approved provider path authorizes paid spend. No paid spend is authorized by this artifact.

Traceability
This req_04 execution specification is grounded in the company launch/context record observed as ev_1790045033627_hyxp0v, which states the relaunch goal, low signup conversion, lack of visitor recognition, owned resources, and no-paid-spend constraint. The revised copy and test plan remain subject to the unresolved decisions listed above.

Revised founder-specific messaging package (req_03)
Primary audience: One-person-company founders and lean-SME operators who are responsible for the work and the coordination around it.
Context: A founder is managing the business while keeping work moving across recurring tasks, tools, and follow-ups.
Headline: "Run your one-person business with an AI manager."
Subhead: "Somebody helps you keep the work moving—so you can spend less time coordinating your business and more time doing the work that matters."
Primary CTA: "Try Somebody"
Supporting message: "You do not need another generic business tool. Somebody is built for founders who are carrying the work and the follow-through themselves."
Recognition cue: "For one-person companies and lean teams."
Rationale: The audience label is explicit rather than generic, directly addressing the verified recognition problem. The message presents an intended use and benefit without asserting measured results.
Traceability: The founder-specific audience and recognition emphasis follow the verified launch context and req_02 diagnosis. Benefit language is a positioning hypothesis, not a measured outcome.
Assumptions/hypotheses: The explicit one-person-company framing will improve visitor recognition; the coordination framing will be more relevant than the former "too many tools" framing; the revised message will improve signup conversion. These must be tested rather than treated as established facts.

Execution-ready relaunch plan (req_04)
Review status: Draft for internal review only. Do not send, publish, or purchase paid distribution from this artifact.
Launch surface: Replace the current headline, subhead, CTA, supporting message, and recognition cue on the launch page after review approval. Keep the current message as the comparison baseline.
Test design: Compare the revised founder-specific message with the current launch message. Hold traffic source, page layout, CTA destination, and measurement window constant where practicable. Record the tested copy version and dates.
Primary success measure: Signup conversion rate for the revised message, compared with the current launch baseline. Define the baseline rate and observation window before launch; do not claim improvement until both periods are measured consistently.
Secondary success measure: Visitor recognition, measured with a short on-page or post-visit response using a predeclared question such as whether the visitor identifies as a one-person-company founder or lean-SME operator. Compare response rates with the current baseline or, if no baseline exists, label the result directional.
Guardrails: Track CTA clicks and completed signups separately; inspect abandonment between click and signup; do not substitute clicks for signups. Do not use paid spend unless an explicit application-approved provider path exists.
Decision rule: Proceed with the revised message if it produces a practically meaningful improvement in completed signup conversion without a material deterioration in recognition or funnel completion. Primary headline: “Run your one-person company with an AI manager.”
Primary subhead: “Somebody keeps the work moving—so you can spend less time coordinating tools, tasks, and follow-ups and more time running the business.”
Recognition line: “Built for founders doing the selling, delivery, admin, and follow-up themselves.”
Value points:
- Turn scattered business work into a clear set of next actions.
- Keep routine follow-ups and operating tasks moving without adding another manager.
- Get practical support across the work a lean company must do every day.
Primary CTA: “Try Somebody”
Secondary CTA: “See how it works”
CTA expectation: The primary CTA should lead directly to the existing signup or trial flow; the secondary CTA should lead to a concise explanation of the workflow and product experience.
Alternate headline options for controlled testing:
A. “Your AI manager for the work behind the business.”
B. “One-person company? Let Somebody run the follow-through.”
Messaging guardrail: Do not claim guaranteed outcomes, full automation, or capabilities not confirmed by the product. Keep “AI manager” as the category description and explain the benefit in concrete founder language.
Assumptions to validate: the product supports the described workflow and follow-up use cases; “Try Somebody” is the correct available conversion path; the audience responds better to “one-person company” than generic “business”; and the secondary CTA destination exists.

Execution-ready launch specification (req_04)
Page order:
1. Primary headline and subhead.
2. Recognition line immediately below the hero.
3. Primary and secondary CTAs.
4. Three value points, using concrete founder language.
5. Short “how it works” explanation with no unsupported capability claims.
6. Repeat the primary CTA.

Consistency checks:
- Audience is consistently “one-person-company founders” (with lean SMEs as adjacent context), not generic “businesses.”
- Problem is consistently operational overload and follow-through, not merely “too many tools.”
- Product role is consistently an AI manager that helps keep work moving; copy must not imply autonomous control beyond verified product capability.
- CTA language and the stated signup objective are aligned.
- The message distinguishes the current baseline from the relaunch and does not present the low-conversion signal as a product promise.

- Confirm the exact signup/trial destination and whether “Try Somebody” is the approved CTA label.
- Confirm which workflow and follow-up capabilities are live; remove any value point not supported by the current product.
- Choose the primary headline and, if testing is possible, define the allocation and test duration without paid spend.
- Confirm whether “one-person company” is the preferred audience term in the page implementation.
- Confirm the measurement owner and the event instrumentation for CTA clicks, signup starts, and completed signups.

Measurement relative to the current launch:
Baseline: the current launch has low signup conversion and visitors do not recognise themselves; the current message uses generic “businesses.”
Primary success measure: completed signup conversion rate from page visitors, compared with the current launch baseline over the same measurement window.
Diagnostic measures: hero-to-CTA click-through rate, signup-start rate, completed-signup rate, and drop-off between signup start and completion. Report absolute rates and percentage-point change versus baseline, not only relative lift.
